arxiv-1603-03165.title: Automated Clustering and Program Repair for Introductory Programming Assignments DOI: 10.1145/3192366.3192387 ISBN: 978-1-4503-5698-5/18/06 Conference: 39th ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation; June 18–22, 2018; Philadelphia, PA, USA Note: Supported by the Austri
arxiv-1603-03165.creator: Sumit Gulwani, Ivan Radiček, Florian Zuleger
arxiv-1603-03165.description: Abstract . Providing feedback on programming assignments is a tedious task for the instructor, and even impossible in large Massive Open Online Courses with thousands of students. Previous research has suggested that program repair techniques can be used to generate feedback in programming education. In this paper, we present a novel fully automated program repair algorithm for introductory programming assignments.

arxiv-2108-07894.title: On the Virality of Animated GIFs on Tumblr
arxiv-2108-07894.creator: Yunseok JangUniversity of MichiganAnn Arbor, MI, Yale SongMicrosoft ResearchRedmond, WAGunhee KimSeoul National UniversitySeoul, Korea
arxiv-2108-07894.description: Abstract Animated GIFs are becoming increasingly popular in online communication. People use them to express emotion, share their interests and enhance (or even replace) short-form texting; they are a new means to tell visual stories. Some creative animated GIFs are highly addictive to watch, and eventually become viral – they circulate rapidly and widely within the network.

arxiv-2306-14708.title: A Simple and Effective Baseline for Attentional Generative Adversarial Networks * Equal contribution. 🖂 Corresponding author.
arxiv-2306-14708.creator: Mingyu Jin, Chong Zhang, Qinkai Yu, Haochen Xue, Xiaobo Jin 🖂, Xi Yang 🖂
arxiv-2306-14708.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mingyu Jin, Chong Zhang, Qinkai Yu, Haochen Xue, Xiaobo Jin 🖂, Xi Yang 🖂. Synthesising a text-to-image model of high-quality images by guiding the generative model through the Text description is an innovative and challenging task.

arxiv-2310-20351.title: Long-range interaction of hydrogen atoms at finite temperatures
arxiv-2310-20351.creator: T. Zalialiutdinov 1,2, D. Solovyev 1,2
arxiv-2310-20351.description: Abstract In this study, we reexamine the long-range interaction between two atoms placed in an equilibrium thermal radiation environment. Employing the formalism of quantum electrodynamics at finite temperatures, we derive an expression for the thermal correction to the interaction potential and explore various asymptotic behaviors.

arxiv-2312-14497.title: The small-scale limit of magnitude and the one-point property
arxiv-2312-14497.creator: Emily Roff, Masahiko Yoshinaga
arxiv-2312-14497.description: Abstract . The magnitude of a metric space is a real-valued function whose parameter controls the scale of the metric. A metric space is said to have the one-point property if its magnitude converges to 1 as the space is scaled down to a point.

arxiv-2403-17497.title: Sharing the Cost of Success: A Game for Evaluating and Learning Collaborative Multi-Agent Instruction Giving and Following Policies
arxiv-2403-17497.description: Abstract In collaborative goal-oriented settings, the participants are not only interested in achieving a successful outcome, but do also implicitly negotiate the effort they put into the interaction (by adapting to each other). In this work, we propose a challenging interactive reference game that requires two players to coordinate on vision and language observations.

arxiv-2412-09373.title: Tunable ultrahigh reflection with broadband via collective atom-atom interaction in waveguide-QED system
arxiv-2412-09373.creator: Xin Wang, Junjun He, Zeyang Liao, M. Suhail Zubairy
arxiv-2412-09373.description: Abstract We present a scheme for achieving broadband complete reflection by constructing photonic bandgap via collective atom-atom interaction in a one-dimensional (1D) waveguide quantum electrodynamics (QED) system. Moreover, we propose several strategies to further expand the ultrahigh reflection windows, including increasing the number of atoms with separations near the Bragg distance and inducing gradient frequency modulation among the atoms.

arxiv-2504-07146.title: VideoSPatS: Video SPatiotemporal Splines for Disentangled Occlusion, Appearance and Motion Modeling and Editing
arxiv-2504-07146.creator: Juan Luis Gonzalez 1, Xu Yao 1, Alex Whelan 1, Kyle Olszewski 1, Hyeongwoo Kim 2, Pablo Garrido 1, 2 Imperial College London, hyeongwoo.kim@imperial.ac.uk
arxiv-2504-07146.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Juan Luis Gonzalez 1, Xu Yao 1, Alex Whelan 1, Kyle Olszewski 1, Hyeongwoo Kim 2, Pablo Garrido 1, 2 Imperial College London, hyeongwoo.kim@imperial.ac.uk. We present an implicit video representation for occlusions, appearance, and motion disentanglement from monocular videos, which we call Video SPatiotemporal Splines ( VideoSPatS ).

arxiv-2601-11499.title: On the Probability of First Success in Differential Evolution: Hazard Identities and Tail Bounds
arxiv-2601-11499.creator: Dimitar Nedanovski, Svetoslav Nenov, Dimitar Pilev
arxiv-2601-11499.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Dimitar Nedanovski, Svetoslav Nenov, Dimitar Pilev. We study first-hitting times in Differential Evolution (DE) through a conditional hazard framework. Instead of analyzing convergence via Markov-chain transition kernels or drift arguments, we express the survival probability of a measurable target set A A as a product of conditional first-hit probabilities (hazards) p t = ℙ ⁡ ( E t ∣ ℱ t − 1 ) p_{t}=\mathbb{P}(E_{t}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t-1}) .

pmc-10696046.title: A review of the research progress on Pinellia ternata (Thunb.) Breit.: Botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity and quality control
pmc-10696046.creator: Ting Zou, Jing Wang, Xu Wu, Kai Yang, Qiao Zhang, Changli Wang, Xiao Wang, Chongbo Zhao
pmc-10696046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Ethnopharmacological relevancePinellia ternata (Thunb.) Breit. is a well-known perennial herb that is used in traditional medicine in China, Japan and Korea. It's drawing worldwide interests in medicinal applications owing such as anti-diarrhea, lipid-lowering, anti-tumor, anti-cough, expectorant, anti-gastric ulcer, etc.Aim of the studyThis review aims to provide useful information on the botany, traditional uses, phytochemistry, pharmacology, toxicity and quality control of Pinellia ternata to help increase its efficiency.

pmc-10714678.title: Systematic review of hematophagous arthropods present in cattle in France
pmc-10714678.creator: Jorian Prudhomme, Jérôme Depaquit, Johanna Fite, Elsa Quillery, Emilie Bouhsira, Emmanuel Liénard
pmc-10714678.description: The arrival of pathogens, whether zoonotic or not, can have a lasting effect on commercial livestock farms, with dramatic health, social and economic consequences. However, available data concerning the arthropod vectors present and circulating on livestock farms in France are still very imprecise, fragmentary, and scattered.

pmc-11351360.title: Exploring and identifying the imaging biomarkers for predicting anti-VEGF treatment response in polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy: a prospective multicenter study
pmc-11351360.creator: Wenfei Zhang, Xingwang Gu, Bing Li, Shulin Liu, Jingyuan Yang, Yuelin Wang, Shiyu Cheng, Lin Lv, Zhiqing Li, Linna Lu, Jinghong Zhang, Qi Zeng, Zefeng Xiao, Guangfeng Liu, Cai Xin, Tianyu Zhang, Yingdan Su, Minyu Chen, Chengshu Wang, Yonkang Cun, Xinyu Zhao, Youxin Chen
pmc-11351360.description: BackgroundPolypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV) is a hemorrhagic fundus disease that can lead to permanent vision loss. Predicting the treatment response to anti-VEGF monotherapy in PCV is consistently challenging. We aimed to conduct a prospective multicenter study to explore and identify the imaging biomarkers for predicting the anti-VEGF treatment response in PCV patients, establish predictive model, and undergo multicenter validation.

pmc-11387077.title: In This Issue on 09-September-2024
pmc-11387077.creator: Jin-Hong Yoo
pmc-11387077.description: the general population and 83.5% of clinicians supported ventilator withdrawal two months after SABI. Support increased to 92% and 94%, respectively, three years after SABI, especially with written Advance Directives. Factors influencing attitudes included spirituality, income, religion, and experience with Advance Directives. The study concluded that legislative adjustments are needed to respect patients’ prior wishes in treatment decisions. 2.

pmc-11438430.title: Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease. Clinical features, imaging findings, conservative treatments and research perspectives: a scoping review
pmc-11438430.creator: Bartosz Wilczyński, Marcin Taraszkiewicz, Karol de Tillier, Maciej Biały, Katarzyna Zorena
pmc-11438430.description: ObjectiveThis review aims to consolidate existing research on the pathogenesis, clinical diagnosis, imaging outcomes, and conservative treatments of Sinding-Larsen-Johansson disease (SLJD), identifying literature gaps.DesignScoping Review.MethodsA comprehensive literature search was conducted across databases including PubMed, Scopus, Medline OVID, Embase, Web of Science, and Grey literature following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) extension for scoping reviews.

pmc-12562091.title: Continuous Optical Biosensing of IL-8 Cancer Biomarker Using a Multimodal Platform
pmc-12562091.creator: A L Hernandez, K Mandal, B Santamaria, S Quintero, M R Dokmeci, V Jucaud, M Holgado, Gou-Jen Wang
pmc-12562091.description: In this work, we used a label-free biosensor that provides optical readouts to perform continuous detection of human interleukin 8 (IL-8), which is especially overexpressed in certain cancers and, thus, could be an effective biomarker for cancer prognosis estimation and therapy evaluation. For this purpose, we engineered a compact, portable, and easy-to-assemble biosensing module device.

pmc-12594502.title: Evaluation of a Digital, Self-Administered, Cognitive Test Battery in Older Adult Patients Undergoing Abdominal Surgery: Nonrandomized Feasibility Trial
pmc-12594502.creator: Anahita Amirpour, Markus Saarijärvi, Jeanette Eckerblad, Gabriela Markovic, Anders Thorell, Ulrica Nilsson, Lina Bergman, Amaryllis Mavragani
pmc-12594502.description: BackgroundOlder adults undergoing surgeries face increased risks of postoperative neurocognitive disorders, which impair cognitive functions. Analog neurocognitive tests are commonly used, but digital tests offer faster, more accessible assessments.ObjectiveThe primary aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a digital cognitive test battery in older adults undergoing abdominal surgery.

pmc-12712533.title: Arthroscopic Biportal Visualization and “Precise Resection” for Recalcitrant Lateral Epicondylitis Lesion
pmc-12712533.creator: Chuan Zhang, Hai-Feng Gu, Jiang-Tao Ma, Ming-Ming Dong, Sui-Zhu Huang
pmc-12712533.description: Refractory lateral epicondylitis poses a significant clinical challenge. In patients with persistent symptoms refractory to conservative treatment, surgical intervention represents an effective approach for achieving durable symptomatic relief. Advances in arthroscopic techniques now offer a more minimally invasive and refined approach.

pmc-13119153.title: Seasonal Dynamics of Skin Microbiota and Metabolites in Transhumant-Grazed Altay Sheep
pmc-13119153.creator: Xin Li, Zihang Qin, Haiyan Wang, Xinyu Tao, Jiangtao Xia, Yukang Zhao, Pengfei Yi, Yunxiao Ma, Xinhao Wang, Xuelian Ma, Na Li, Qi Zhong, Gang Yao
pmc-13119153.description: To explore the seasonal variation patterns of the skin microecology of Altay sheep under transhumant grazing conditions, skin swabs were collected from 60 free-grazing Altay sheep at seasonal transition nodes in the Altay region. Metagenomic sequencing combined with untargeted metabolomics was used to characterize their bacterial community structure, functional pathways, and metabolite profiles.

pmc-13155575.title: A pumpless liver-adipose model for studying metabolic dysfunction and drug responses
pmc-13155575.creator: Zeinab Ebrahimian, Fatemeh Kalalinia, Amir Reza Ameri, Hossein Hosseinzadeh, Bibi Marjan Razavi, Seyed Ali Mousavi Shaegh, Santhi Silambanan, Santhi Silambanan, Santhi Silambanan
pmc-13155575.description: Metabolic dysfunction is a primary driver of chronic diseases, such as obesity and type 2 diabetes. Developing in vitro models allows to understand metabolic mechanisms and develop effective treatments. To this end, a pumpless open-top co-culture (POCC) device to simulate liver–adipose tissue interactions was developed. The POCC comprises a four-chamber bioreactor with an open-top configuration and an easy-to-assemble cover cap.

pmc-13212698.title: Unraveling BCR Repertoire Diversity and its Impact on Glucocorticoid Therapy in Pediatric Idiopathic Nephrotic Syndrome
pmc-13212698.creator: Yeping Luo, Chan Zou, Xinjie Yu, Chengxian Guo, Hongmei Dai, Jie Huang, Mai Xun, Cuirong Duan, Song Li, Zhihui Li, Guoping Yang
pmc-13212698.description: AimIdiopathic nephrotic syndrome (INS) is the most common glomerular disease in children, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Although glucocorticoids (GC) are the first-line treatment, approximately 10% of INS cases are steroid-resistant (SRNS), and 50% may progress to refractory nephrotic syndrome (RNS). B cells play a crucial role in INS pathogenesis, treatment, and prognosis.

pmc-13646673.title: Trichomes in Plant Defence, Development and Metabolic Integration Under Environmental Stress
pmc-13646673.creator: Debdatta Chatterjee, Madhabi Das, Sanjib Patra, Srijib Chatterjee, Amit Roy, Arunava Mandal
pmc-13646673.description: Among various plant defence strategies, trichomes are tiny hair‐like structures on the epidermis that aid in defence, environmental adaptation and the production of valuable secondary metabolites. This review features trichomes as frontline guards for plant survival, integrating their structural, physiological and metabolic roles in safeguarding against environmental adversity.
